name: Benign Paroxysmal Positional Vertigo
definition: Brief recurrent positional vertigo caused by displaced otoconia within a semicircular canal, most commonly the posterior canal.

typical: Seconds-long vertigo triggered by head position
Turning in bed or looking up provokes symptoms

redFlags.item: New severe headache or neck pain

core: Supine roll test for horizontal canal

investigations.MRI: MRI is not routine unless central features are present.

green: Vestibular rehabilitation when residual imbalance persists
amber: Avoid inappropriate repositioning in unstable cervical spine or serious vascular/neurological conditions.
red: Urgent red-flag features override routine conservative or Ayurvedic pathways.

ayurvedaFramework.text: Bhrama phenotype may be documented only after excluding central/urgent causes.

patientEducation.summary: Brief recurrent positional vertigo caused by displaced otoconia within a semicircular canal, most commonly the posterior canal.
patientEducation.urgent: Seek urgent assessment for acute/progressive neurological deficit, sphincter change, severe infection/systemic illness, major trauma, vascular compromise or other listed red flags.
